The corners and mid-points of the sides of a triangle are named using the distinct
letters P, Q, R, S, T and U, but not necessarily in the same order. Consider the
following statements:
 The line joining P and R is parallel to the line joining Q and S.
 P is placed on the side opposite to the corner T.
 S and U cannot be placed on the same side.
Which one of the following statements is correct based on the above
information?

options.A: P cannot be placed at a corner
options.B: S cannot be placed at a corner
options.C: U cannot be placed at a mid-point
options.D: R cannot be placed at a corner

questions.subtopic: Transformation of shapes: translation, rotation, scaling, mirroring, assembling, and grouping
questions.explaination: In a triangle, a segment connecting two midpoints is parallel to the opposite side joining two vertices. Between segments $PR$ and $QS$, one must connect two corners and the other two midpoints. If $S$ were a corner, then $Q$ and $S$ would both be corners, leaving $P$ and $R$ as midpoints, which violates the condition that $S$ and $U$ cannot share a side while $P$ opposes corner $T$. Thus, $S$ cannot be placed at a corner.

Let U = {1, 2, . . . , n}, where n is a large positive integer greater than 1000. Let
k be a positive integer less than n. Let A, B be subsets of U with |A| = |B| = k
and A ∩B = ∅. We say that a permutation of U separates A from B if one of the
following is true.
- All members of A appear in the permutation before any of the members of B.
- All members of B appear in the permutation before any of the members of A.
How many permutations of U separate A from B?

options.A: n!

questions.subtopic: Combinatorics: counting, recurrence relations, generating functions
questions.explaination: There are 2 orderings for which block appears first ($A$ before $B$ or $B$ before $A$). There are $\binom{n}{2k}$ ways to choose the positions in the permutation for elements of $A \cup B$. The first $k$ chosen positions must contain elements of the first set ($k!$ permutations) and the next $k$ positions contain elements of the second set ($k!$ permutations). The remaining $n - 2k$ elements can be arranged in any of the $(n - 2k)!$ remaining positions. Total valid permutations $= 2 \binom{n}{2k} (n - 2k)! (k!)^2$.

A processor has 16 integer registers (R0, R1, .. , R15) and 64 floating point registers (F0,
F1,… , F63). It uses a 2-byte instruction format. There are four categories of instructions:
Type-1, Type-2, Type-3, and Type-4. Type-1 category consists of four instructions, each
with 3 integer register operands (3Rs). Type-2 category consists of eight instructions, each
with 2 floating point register operands (2Fs). Type-3 category consists of fourteen
instructions, each with one integer register operand and one floating point register operand
(1R+1F). Type-4 category consists of N instructions, each with a floating point register
operand (1F).

The maximum value of N is __________.
questions.subtopic: Machine instructions and addressing modes
questions.explaination: A 16-bit instruction space has $2^{16} = 65536$ encodings. Type-1: 4 instructions with $3 \times 4\text{-bit}$ registers consume $4 \times 2^{12} = 16384$. Type-2: 8 instructions with $2 \times 6\text{-bit}$ registers consume $8 \times 2^{12} = 32768$. Type-3: 14 instructions with 4-bit and 6-bit registers consume $14 \times 2^{10} = 14336$. Remaining encodings $= 65536 - (16384 + 32768 + 14336) = 2048$. Each Type-4 instruction uses one 6-bit register ($2^6 = 64$ encodings). Thus, maximum $N = 2048 / 64 = 32$.

that order 10 times (i.e., PQRSPQRS…). Hence, there are 40 accesses to data cache
altogether. Assume that the data cache is initially empty and no other data words are
accessed by the program. The addresses of the first bytes of P, Q, R, and S are
0xA248, 0xC28A, 0xCA8A, and 0xA262, respectively. For the execution of the

options.A: Every access to S is a hit.
options.B: Once P is brought to the cache it is never evicted.
options.C: At the end of the execution only R and S reside in the cache.

Once P is loaded, S is also present in line 9, so every access to S is a hit (A is TRUE) and P/S are never evicted (B is TRUE).
